questions.problem:
Two biased coins are tossed several times. The results are recorded below. Based on this data, if the random variable $X$ represents the number of heads obtained on a random toss, what is $\text{SD}[X]?$

| Number of heads | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frequency | $4$ | $12$ | $9$ |
questions.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ To do this, we divide each frequency by the total, which is $4+12+9=25.$ We get the following result:

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{4}{25}$ | $\frac{12}{25}$ | $\frac{9}{25}$ |

Now, we compute $\text{E}[X]$ by summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2) \\  & =0(\frac{4}{25})+1(\frac{12}{25})+2(\frac{9}{25}) \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2) \\  & =0(\frac{4}{25})+1(\frac{12}{25})+4(\frac{9}{25}) \\  & =\frac{48}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{48}{25}-{(\frac{6}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{48}{25}-\frac{36}{25} \\  & =\frac{12}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{12}{25}} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Two fair  four-sided dice are rolled and $X$ is the absolute difference of their scores. The probability mass function $f(x)$ of $X$ is shown in the table below. What is $\text{SD}[X]?$ 

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ |
questions.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3) \\  & =0(\frac{1}{4})+1(\frac{3}{8})+2(\frac{1}{4})+3(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & =0(\frac{1}{4})+1(\frac{3}{8})+4(\frac{1}{4})+9(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-{(\frac{5}{4})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}-\frac{25}{16} \\  & =\frac{15}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{15}{16}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{15}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $X$ be the number obtained by a spinner with five sections labeled $-2,-1,0,1,2.$ The probability mass function $f(x)$ of $X$ is shown in the table below. What is $\text{Var}[X]?$

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ | $\frac{3}{16}$ |
questions.worked_solution:
We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =(-2)\cdot f(-2)+(-1)\cdot f(-1)+0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2) \\  & =(-2)(\frac{1}{8})+(-1)(\frac{1}{4})+0(\frac{3}{8})+1(\frac{1}{16})+2(\frac{3}{16}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & =(-2)^{2}\cdot f(-2)+(-1)^{2}\cdot f(-1)+{0}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2) \\  & =4(\frac{1}{8})+1(\frac{1}{4})+0(\frac{3}{8})+1(\frac{1}{16})+4(\frac{3}{16}) \\  & =\frac{25}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{25}{16}-{(-\frac{1}{16})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{25}{16}-\frac{1}{256} \\  & =\frac{400}{256}-\frac{1}{256} \\  & =\frac{399}{256}.\end{aligned}
$$
